pattern: wrapping an imperative helper as a reactive primitive
why: the primitive inevitably re-exposes the imperative helper as a method
instead: widen the helper's args to T|Node<T>; let the caller opt into reactive control

why: ctx can never observe the true absence-of-DATA state
instead: fix the upstream to stop eager-emitting; use prevData[i]===undefined as the never-emitted detector

why: deadlock≠thrash confusion; the process group can't be killed cleanly
instead: one target at a time; bounded -j; kill by process group; direct log + DONE sentinel

why: the design session task table lags the code; opening a 9Q on a stale premise
instead: grep the named symbols + check the landed marker; surface the stale premise as a HALT

pattern: making architectural decisions on your own initiative
why: silently picking a side masks a spec↔code conflict
instead: surface the conflict for the user to call; review multi-file rewrites file by file

pattern: marking active/superseded with prose inside the archive
why: markers rot; active and superseded end up mixed in one directory
instead: split active/archive into physical directories; put the state in a jsonl status field

pattern: canonical responsibility split across multiple documents
why: the sequencer/decision-log is scattered in many places, causing migration-period confusion
instead: a single canonical per responsibility; decisions in a single D# sequence

pattern: letting an adapter, queue or persistence layer independently decide semantic retry, fallback, admission, recovery or effect commitment
why: the hidden mechanism becomes a shadow workflow and invalidates the declared Causal WYSIWYG scope
instead: keep semantic policy and decisions graph-visible; let host-private adapters perform only declared mechanics and return bounded exact outcomes

pattern: minting a new D# for each attempt, rerun or additional-spend approval while the same semantic question and work episode remain open
why: attempt mechanics and one-time human authorization are not new durable decisions; encoding them as D# creates permanent cognitive burden, makes repeated failure look like architectural progress and scatters one stalled objective across records that later reviewers must reconstruct
instead: keep one durable D# for the unchanged semantic contract and one owner-local work item or evaluation charter for the unchanged work episode; record attempts, incidents, repairs, receipts and evidence under non-decision coordinates. A rerun or additional spend still requires fresh explicit human authorization, but that authorization must link to the existing work or charter and must not mint a D#. Create a new durable D# only when the semantic contract or success criteria materially change; stop, compress failed evidence, name the blocker and complete no-network qualification before requesting another run
